___note: Dedicated fixture for tests/harness/askcard.spec.ts. It must NOT live in the shared tests/harness/fixtures/llm dir: createMockLlm (packages/agent-harness-core/src/mock-llm.ts) tries every SEQUENCE fixture in a directory before any responses fixture, so council.json's positional sequence would win and this wildcard would never be reached. It is also separate from tests/harness/fixtures/llm-askcard, which tests/integration/askcard-parked-run.test.ts still uses to park the RETAINED legacy clarify card under its infrastructure-role entry; that fixture's model stream must stay a plain reply.
___why_two_blocks: The TUI has two independent mock hooks. `model` feeds globalThis.__muonroiMockModel (src/providers/runtime.ts) — the AI-SDK path used by main's turn and by PIL's model-first classifier. `responses` feeds globalThis.__muonroiMockLlm (src/council/llm.ts getMockLlm) — the path EVERY council generate/debate/research call short-circuits through, including the detached background council that `--force-council` launches.
___how_the_card_appears: Since b014c9b9 the TUI main agent is the orchestrator role: `/ideal` launches the forced council as a durable background job (orchestrator.ts runProductLoopV1, executionRole === 'orchestrator' branch) and hands the request to main's own turn. That council runs headless (src/index.ts council delegation: skipClarification + suppressPreDebateCards), so it can never open a card. Main asks the human through its ask_user tool instead (src/tools/registry.ts ask_user; use-app-logic setAskUserHandler renders CouncilQuestionCard under <Semantic id="askcard" role="dialog"> and emits askcard-open phase=ask-user). Stream round 0 is therefore main calling ask_user; the tool BLOCKS until answered, which keeps the card on screen for the navigation test. Round 1 is the reply main gives once answered.
